_comment: Skeleton for the two new gates introduced by the 2026-10-15 QC policy. Fields marked TODO need the rebuilt image; everything else is already measured or read from the package. Feed this into quality-review-filled.json once the image is rebuilt.

windows_image_policy._label: Windows 镜像不早于 2019，优先 2025，禁止 Nano Server/Server Core 和额外裁剪

evidence: The FROM line names the full Windows Server runtime, not servercore and not nanoserver.

Measured remotely against mcr.microsoft.com: windows/server:ltsc2022 has 2 layers totalling 4176 MB; windows/servercore:ltsc2022 (2066 MB) and windows/nanoserver:ltsc2022 (116 MB) are the trimmed families and are forbidden; windows/server:ltsc2022 (4176 MB) is also complete but carries build 20348, so this image is demonstrably the complete (untrimmed) family rather than a trimmed one.
ltsc2025 carries os.version 10.0.26100, which is the same build as the buyer Windows 11 hosts, so it matches the target environment instead of merely staying compatible with it.
TODO: record the container-side os.version and Confirm-SecureBootUEFI-equivalent build check from the rebuilt image.

notes: Buyer environment is Windows build 20348/ltsc2022 with Hyper-V isolation; the base matches that build, so no version downgrade was needed.
Server Core was the previous base and is explicitly forbidden by current-project-policy.md item 1; the switch to windows/server is the only compliant option.

nested_virtualization._label: 实际使用嵌套虚拟化，外层 VM/扩展暴露/内层运行和当前 jobs 证据完整
nested_virtualization._reason: This host is a physical Lenovo workstation (Manufacturer LENOVO, Model 90NA001PCD, BIOS O4HKT30A). Docker Desktop runs Windows containers with --isolation=hyperv, which is one layer only: physical host -> Hyper-V container. The current policy states that running a Hyper-V container directly on a physical host is still a single layer, so the required L0 -> L1 -> L2 chain does not exist here. Per the nested-virtualization gate this cannot be recorded as PASS and must not be silently downgraded.
nested_virtualization._what_is_needed: A host that is itself a guest VM (L1) with virtualization extensions exposed, on which the inner hypervisor starts the Windows container or VM (L2) that actually runs the task. Evidence required: outer Get-VMProcessor ExposeVirtualizationExtensions, L1 capability probe, inner start logs with VM/container id, and job binding to this task hash and image digest.
